svg.aria-label: Installing the cached codegen backend by rename: every rustc that compiles a kernel maps the one shared .so; std::fs::copy truncated that inode under them and killed the running compiler; copying to a sibling temporary and renaming it over the name leaves the old inode to its mappers

text.style: font: 600 17px var(--sans); fill: var(--fg); white-space: pre

svg.text: Installing the cached backend by rename, not in place

text.style: font: 400 12.5px var(--sans); fill: var(--muted); white-space: pre

svg.text: Every rustc that compiles a kernel maps the shared 428 MB librustc_codegen_cuda.so. std::fs::copy rewrote that inode under them; a sibling temporary plus rename leaves it alone.

text.style: font: 600 11px var(--sans); fill: var(--muted); white-space: pre

svg.text: THE SETUP (one file, many readers, three writers)

svg.text: // = librustc_codegen_cuda.so.<pid>.<nonce>.tmp

svg.text: fs::rename(&tmp, &so_path)?; // atomic, same directory

text.style: font: 400 10.2px var(--mono); fill: var(--fg); white-space: pre

svg.text: write_toolchain_fingerprint(..); record_source_rev(..);

svg.text: Why the rename is safe and the copy was not

text.style: font: 400 11.5px var(--sans); fill: var(--fg); white-space: pre

svg.text: rename(2) swaps the directory entry. A mapped inode stays allocated until its last mapper exits, and a new open sees the complete new file.

text.style: font: 400 11.5px var(--sans); fill: var(--fg); white-space: pre

svg.text: std::fs::copy reopened that inode with O_TRUNC under every mapping: pages past the new end are gone (SIGBUS), and so are the mapping's private pages (SIGSEGV).

text.style: font: 400 11.5px var(--sans); fill: var(--muted); white-space: pre

svg.text: Measured: a rustc with the 428 MB backend mapped, killed 5/5 in place (identical bytes), finished 5/5 by rename; an mmap reader of a 64 MB install, SIGBUS 6/6 before, 0/6 after.
